title: Hybrid seat + usage — quick back-of-envelope math
body:
Context:
- Quick personal scratchpad evaluating a hybrid pricing model: small base seat fee + usage overage. Aim: simpler entry price for SMBs, predictable revenue for us, still capture heavy users.

Goals for this memo:
- Produce a couple of example tiers and unit-econ back-of-envelope numbers.
- Surface sensitivity to token cost, active users, and avg tokens per user.
- Flag tricky edge cases (burst users, bots, trial abuse).

Assumptions (ballpark / adjustable):
- Our marginal model serving cost to Redwood (hosted API) = $0.0006 per 1k tokens (net infra + amortized model licensing).
- Platform + support + infra overhead allocated to product = $0.0004 per 1k tokens.
- Total marginal cost per 1k tokens = $0.001. (Round friendly.)
- Target gross margin target for hosted plans = 60% (so price per 1k tokens should be ~2.5x cost).
- Average MAU per SMB = 120 users. Active users (monthly) = 25% of MAU -> 30 DAUs-ish.
- Example heavy user profile: 5 power users generate 50% of tokens.

Simple baseline: pure usage price to hit margin
- If cost = $0.001 per 1k, target price = $0.0025 per 1k (rounded to $0.0025).
- For 1M tokens/month: cost = $1, price = $2.50, gross margin = 60%.

Hybrid seat+usage sketch (3 examples):
1) Starter: $15 / seat-month (billed per user), includes 50k tokens seat credit, $0.003 per 1k tokens overage.
   - Effective included compute value per seat = 50k tokens -> price-equivalent at pure usage $0.125 (if $0.0025/1k) -> but main value is predictable.
   - For a 10-seat team: base = $150/mo, includes 500k tokens. If consumed 1.5M tokens total -> overage = 1.0M -> overage charge = $3.00 -> total $153 -> blended token price ~0.102 per 1k (this shows heavy usage is inexpensive in this simple example).
   - Problem: generous included credit dilutes unit economics if heavy users. Need guardrails.

2) Pro: $30 / seat-month, includes 200k tokens seat credit, $0.0028 per 1k overage.
   - 20 seats -> base = $600/mo includes 4M tokens. For many customer profiles this covers normal usage. Heavy usage above that quickly becomes overage.
   - If the customer has large power users (5 users each 1M tokens/mo) we need either quotaing or per-tenant volume pricing.

3) Usage-first (for scale customers): $0 / seat, $0.002 / 1k tokens up to 100M, volume tiers below cost + seat fee for SLA.
   - For commitments (dedicated), we can offer lower $/1k because we reserve capacity and get predictable throughput.

Unit econ worked example (mid-sized customer):
- 50 seats, average 80k tokens/seat/month = 4M tokens/month total.
- Using Pro above: base = 50 * $30 = $1,500 includes 10M tokens (since 200k * 50 = 10M). Customer won't pay overages.
- Our marginal cost on 4M tokens = 4M/1k * $0.001 = $4.
- Revenue = $1,500. Gross margin ~ (1500 - 4)/1500 = 99.7% (obviously ridiculous because seat fee is mostly margin; this highlights risk of underpricing seats relative to included credits).
- Takeaway: seat fees can be a huge margin lever but need to align included tokens to realistic usage or convert excess usage to seats/quotas.

Sensitivity notes:
- If marginal cost were actually $0.002/1k (due to large context lengths or expensive LLM), the pure-usage plan economics flip; seats protect us.
- Heavy tails: a few users producing 90% of tokens break seat-credit assumptions. Mitigation: soft caps, per-app rate limiting, or automatic volume discounts that kick in with higher price per token.

Pricing levers to consider (operations + biz/dev tradeoffs):
- Included token credits per seat (low-> encourages seats; high -> easier sale but costly).
- Overage $/1k that decreases with committed spend (volume tiers).
- Per-seat feature flags (e.g., seats that include streaming, enhanced SLA) to justify higher seat price.
- Session or concurrency limits to control real-time cost.
- Trial credits that are token-limited and expire to prevent abuse.

Edge cases and guardrails:
- API keys used for server-side bots -> need different pricing (bot accounts) or require dedicated capacity.
- Burst campaigns (one-week spike) -> autoscaling costs; could bill per-peak or require burst add-on.
- Fraud: multi-tenant usage from one key; need telemetry + rate limiting + billing detection.

Open questions / next actions:
- Run small simulation with actual distribution (gamma) for tokens per user from telemetry: estimate 10th/50th/90th percentiles.
- Recommended quick experiments: 1) propose 3 seat tiers with included tokens reduced by 50% from naive assumption; 2) Add clear soft-cap rules and overage pricing; 3) Pilot with 10 SMB customers for 2 months to collect real blended rates.

Notes-to-self:
- Avoid over-indexing on included tokens in first pass. Seats should primarily sell predictability and multi-user management, not be a disguised free token pool.
- Consider a "seat credit conversion" metric: X seats = Y tokens equivalence (for sales math).
- Keep an eye on churn signals when moving from free credits to paid seats.

Rough TL;DR:
- Hybrid seat+usage works if included credits are conservative and overages/volume tiers are sane. Seats give predictable revenue and high apparent gross margin but can hide mismatched unit economics for heavy-tail users. Run a telemetry-backed sim before firming numbers.

-- Ava
